newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court quashes last B Band disqualifications.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court quashes last B Band disqualifications.

text.p: A Brazilian high court Tuesday ruled that the final two groups barred from bidding for one of the country's most attractive cellular Band B concessions should be able to participate in ther auction, a spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman for the Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ) said the court decided the Telet and MCOM Wireless groups could bid for the metropolitan Sao Paulo service area, overturning their disqualification by the Ministry of Communications.
Telet includes Canadian operators Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc, and Telesystem. In addition in consists of Brazil's Banco do Brasil, Brazilian pension funds, the Opportunity Bank and Citibank.
The MCOM Wireless group is made up of Mexico's Telmex, the investment wing of Brazil's Banco Garantia and Comcast of the United States.
Earlier Tuesday, the STJ overturned the disqualifications of three other groups and on Monday it ruled another should be able to bid.
The STJ spokeswoman said that in all cases the court had found that the Ministry of Communications' grounds for barring the bidders had been "too excessive in its formalities".

The government was due Wednesday to open bids for what many regard as potentially the most lucrative of the 10 concession areas, the Sao Paulo metropolitan area. Bids for the Bahia and Sergipe state area were also due to be opened.
